title: Climate Dynamics, Modeling & Prediction
credential: Graduate Certificate of Completion in Climate Dynamics, Modeling & Prediction

weeksData.title: Earth System Energy Balance & Climate Scales
days: Define weather, climate, variability, prediction and projection across Earth-system timescales.
Derive global energy-balance terms, spherical averaging and unit-consistent flux budgets.
Annotate top-of-atmosphere shortwave and longwave fields in Solanar TraceLab, preserving source and interpretation layers.
Run a conceptual zero-dimensional energy-balance experiment and test albedo/emissivity sensitivity.
Defend a source-grounded energy-budget statement that separates observation, assumption, inference and uncertainty.

weeksData.title: Radiative Transfer, Forcing & Response
days: Study absorption, emission, optical depth, greenhouse behavior and the physical meaning of radiative forcing.
Connect differential energy tendencies to forcing-response equations and compute idealized transient/equilibrium responses.
Use TraceLab to interpret vertical or spectral radiation graphics and identify where model assumptions enter.
Run controlled forcing experiments and compare the conceptual model response with linear-response expectations.
Defend the distinctions among forcing, feedback, efficacy, response and uncertainty.

weeksData.title: Hydrologic Cycle, Moisture & Energetic Constraints
days: Trace evaporation, atmospheric transport, condensation, precipitation, runoff and storage through the coupled hydrologic cycle.
Quantify latent-heat transport, moisture budgets, anomalies and percent change with correct baselines.
Use TraceLab to diagnose regional or global moisture and precipitation anomaly patterns.
Build a water-energy pathway schematic and test how warming can alter moisture capacity without uniform precipitation change.
Submit a hydrologic-cycle memo with explicit variable definitions, units, baselines and confidence limits.

weeksData.title: Atmospheric General Circulation
days: Analyze Hadley, Ferrel and polar overturning, jets, eddy transports and angular-momentum constraints.
Relate pressure-gradient, Coriolis, hydrostatic and advective terms to large-scale circulation balances.
Trace climatological winds, jets and overturning signatures on reanalysis maps in TraceLab.
Use OHMIC CAD Studio to construct a meridional circulation cross-section with forces, fluxes and scale assumptions.
Defend how circulation redistributes heat and moisture and why zonal-mean diagrams cannot represent every local process.

weeksData.title: Ocean Circulation, Heat Storage & Overturning
days: Study wind-driven gyres, Ekman transport, geostrophic flow, overturning, stratification and ocean heat uptake.
Compute idealized heat content, transport and mixed-layer/deep-ocean response timescales.
Annotate SST, ocean-heat-content or circulation fields in TraceLab and separate surface pattern from subsurface storage.
Use OHMIC CAD Studio to build an ocean-basin cross-section showing surface forcing, overturning branches and heat reservoirs.
Write an ocean-climate interpretation separating circulation change, heat uptake, internal variability and forced response.

weeksData.title: Rotating Stratified Fluid Dynamics
days: Review vorticity, potential vorticity, stratification, buoyancy frequency, deformation radius and Rossby-number reasoning.
Derive selected rotating-fluid relationships, state approximations and perform dimensional checks.
Use TraceLab to identify balanced structures, fronts, jets and characteristic scales in atmospheric/oceanic fields.
Compare geostrophic, hydrostatic and ageostrophic interpretations using controlled calculation cases.
Complete a whiteboard/oral defense of scale analysis and the consequences of neglected terms.
weeksData.checkpoint: Qualifying Checkpoint I · Climate Foundations & Fluid Dynamics

weeksData.title: Coupled Atmosphere–Ocean Feedbacks
days: Study two-way atmosphere-ocean coupling, memory, flux feedbacks, delayed response and coupled instability.
Represent simplified coupled systems with differential equations, matrices and stability reasoning.
Annotate paired SST, wind and pressure anomalies in TraceLab to diagnose plausible coupling pathways.
Run a conceptual coupled-response experiment and test sensitivity to damping and coupling strength.
Construct a causal-chain defense distinguishing correlation, mechanistic consistency and demonstrated causation.

weeksData.title: ENSO Dynamics & Tropical Pacific Predictability
days: Examine Bjerknes feedback, thermocline adjustment, recharge/discharge concepts and ENSO diversity.
Analyze Niño indices, lead-lag relationships, autocorrelation and simplified oscillator behavior.
Compare SST, wind, thermocline and precipitation anomalies across ENSO phases in TraceLab.
Build a prediction-evidence matrix separating initialized forecast information, statistical climatology and hindsight.
Present an ENSO briefing with uncertainty, teleconnection limits and calibrated claims about predictability.

weeksData.title: Monsoons, ITCZ Migration & Tropical Hydroclimate
days: Analyze energetic controls on ITCZ position, land-ocean thermal contrast, monsoon circulations and seasonal migration.
Quantify seasonal composites, area-weighted precipitation and energy metrics.
Trace convergence zones, rainfall maxima and circulation anomalies in TraceLab across seasons or years.
Construct a seasonal hydroclimate schematic linking radiation, land response, circulation and moisture transport.
Defend why monsoon change cannot be reduced to a single temperature metric.

weeksData.title: Teleconnections, Annular Modes & Pattern Analysis
days: Study teleconnections, stationary waves, annular modes and the limits of named climate indices.
Use covariance matrices, eigenvectors and principal-component concepts to understand EOF analysis.
Annotate a leading spatial mode and associated time series in TraceLab, including sign and sampling caveats.
Compare EOF-derived patterns with physically defined indices and test sensitivity to domain and normalization.
Write a methods defense explaining what an EOF reveals and what it cannot prove physically.

weeksData.title: Cryosphere, Snow, Sea Ice & Ice–Albedo Feedback
days: Study snow, sea ice, glaciers and ice sheets as radiative, dynamical and mass-balance components of climate.
Quantify anomaly and trend while separating area, extent, thickness, mass and energy concepts.
Annotate sea-ice, snow or ice-mass anomaly maps in TraceLab and document spatial heterogeneity.
Use OHMIC CAD Studio to build a labeled ice-ocean-atmosphere cross-section with energy and mass pathways.
Submit a cryosphere feedback assessment with observational constraints and uncertainty statements.

weeksData.title: Land Surface, Biosphere & Carbon–Climate Coupling
days: Analyze land energy balance, soil moisture, vegetation, evapotranspiration, carbon reservoirs and atmosphere-land coupling.
Build simplified reservoir/flux equations and evaluate residence-time reasoning.
Annotate drought, vegetation, land-surface or carbon-flux anomaly fields in TraceLab.
Run a conceptual reservoir response exercise and examine feedback sign and response time.
Defend a carbon-budget statement using strict stock-versus-flow accounting.
weeksData.checkpoint: Qualifying Checkpoint II · Coupled Variability & Earth-System Feedbacks

weeksData.title: Clouds, Aerosols & Feedback Uncertainty
days: Study cloud radiative effects, aerosol forcing, microphysics, parameterization and uncertainty pathways.
Separate observational, parametric, structural and internal-variability uncertainty in quantitative cases.
Annotate cloud/aerosol forcing or response fields in TraceLab with full provenance.
Compare two conceptual parameterizations and identify conclusions robust to uncertain parameter choices.
Produce an uncertainty ledger that records direction, magnitude, confidence and competing interpretations.

weeksData.title: Paleoclimate Evidence & Natural Forcing
days: Study proxies, age models, orbital forcing, volcanism, solar variability and paleoclimate constraints.
Analyze irregular sampling, calibration, chronology uncertainty and time-scale mismatch in proxy records.
Compare reconstructed and simulated patterns or diagnostic figures in TraceLab.
Construct an evidence-chain diagram from proxy measurement through calibration, chronology and reconstruction.
Defend a paleoclimate inference while marking direct evidence, proxy inference and model-assisted interpretation.

weeksData.title: Climate Sensitivity, Feedback Analysis & Emergent Constraints
days: Compare equilibrium and transient climate response concepts and the physical basis of feedback decomposition.
Calculate feedback-parameter relationships and propagate uncertainty through simplified response estimates.
Annotate forcing-response and feedback diagnostics in TraceLab, including method assumptions.
Use Sagaen Pro Art to create a publication-quality explanatory plate without altering scientific scales or uncertainty.
Critique an emergent-constraint argument for mechanism, independence, selection effects and out-of-sample credibility.

weeksData.title: Detection, Attribution & Forced Response
days: Distinguish detection from attribution and study fingerprints, counterfactual framing, forcing experiments and internal variability.
Analyze signal-to-noise, regression, covariance structure and ensemble means in attribution problems.
Compare observed and simulated patterns in TraceLab and mark regions that affect interpretation.
Design a controlled attribution experiment with candidate forcings, counterfactuals and falsifiable comparison criteria.
Deliver an attribution defense that states alternative explanations and evidence that would weaken the conclusion.

weeksData.title: Observations, Reanalysis & Climate Data Integrity
days: Study observing systems, reanalysis, homogenization, gridding, missing data, representativeness and metadata.
Quantify anomalies, climatologies, trend sensitivity, sampling error and serial correlation.
Compare observational products or reanalysis fields in TraceLab and annotate meaningful discrepancies.
Perform a reproducibility audit covering source, variable, units, aggregation, grid, transformations and version.
Write a graduate methods-section data-integrity statement.

weeksData.title: Semester I Synthesis · Coupled Climate Dynamics
days: Synthesize energy balance, circulation, coupling, feedbacks, variability and observation into one Earth-system framework.
Complete cumulative quantitative derivations spanning budgets, dynamics, covariance and uncertainty.
Produce a TraceLab multi-panel diagnostic from an assigned climate case with source/annotation separation preserved.
Construct a systems-level atmosphere-ocean-land-cryosphere model plate without implying false precision.
Complete the Semester I written/oral synthesis and identify unresolved questions that motivate Semester II modeling.
weeksData.checkpoint: Qualifying Checkpoint III · Semester I Comprehensive

weeksData.title: Model Hierarchies: Energy-Balance to Earth-System Models
days: Compare conceptual, box, energy-balance, intermediate-complexity, GCM and Earth-system model hierarchies by scientific purpose.
Derive a time-dependent energy-balance model and connect heat capacity, feedback and response time.
Use TraceLab to compare outputs from models of differing complexity without treating complexity as automatic accuracy.
Use OHMIC CAD Studio to build a hierarchy plate marking resolved, parameterized and prescribed processes.
Defend model choice as a function of hypothesis, scale, data, cost and uncertainty.

weeksData.title: Grids, Resolution, Discretization & Numerical Representation
days: Study horizontal/vertical grids, coordinates, resolution, truncation, numerical diffusion and conservation requirements.
Analyze discretization error, stability concepts and spherical-grid geometry through finite-difference and matrix views.
Annotate gridded model fields in TraceLab and separate resolved structure from interpolation artifacts.
Use OHMIC CAD Studio to diagram a model mesh and document grid-cell geometry and scale.
Write a resolution audit naming resolved, under-resolved and parameterized phenomena.

weeksData.title: Coupled GCM/ESM Architecture & Conservation
days: Examine atmosphere, ocean, land, sea-ice, biogeochemical and coupler components of comprehensive models.
Audit conservation of mass, energy and tracers across component exchanges.
Use TraceLab to compare component outputs and identify physically coherent cross-component signals.
Build an OHMIC CAD model-architecture diagram with flux directions, coupling frequency and state variables.
Defend why coupling strategy, parameterization and conservation diagnostics matter to scientific interpretation.

weeksData.title: Spin-Up, Control Climate, Drift & Initialization
days: Study equilibration, control simulations, model drift, initialization shock and slow ocean/cryosphere adjustment.
Quantify drift, baseline stability and time-dependent bias using trend and residual diagnostics.
Annotate control-run diagnostics in TraceLab and distinguish drift from forced response.
Run a two-reservoir conceptual spin-up experiment and test sensitivity to initial conditions and slow timescales.
Write a model-readiness memo stating whether the simulation is sufficiently equilibrated for the proposed inference.

weeksData.title: Initial-Condition, Parametric & Structural Ensembles
days: Distinguish initial-condition, perturbed-parameter, multi-model and scenario ensembles and what uncertainty each can sample.
Use ensemble means, spread, covariance and quantiles without conflating ensemble spread with total uncertainty.
Annotate ensemble maps or plumes in TraceLab, marking robust sign and low-agreement regions.
Run the Solanar ensemble experiment and test how ensemble size affects sample mean and spread.
Defend an ensemble claim with explicit language about what is and is not represented.

weeksData.title: Model Evaluation, Bias, Skill & Rapid Evaluation
days: Study process-oriented evaluation, climatological bias, variability, extremes, conservation and out-of-sample tests.
Calculate bias, RMSE, correlation and distributional diagnostics with appropriate caveats.
Compare model and observation fields in TraceLab and annotate spatially coherent biases.
Design a reproducible evaluation dashboard specification inspired by rapid-evaluation principles.
Complete a model-evaluation defense explaining why no single scalar score establishes universal model quality.
weeksData.checkpoint: Qualifying Checkpoint IV · Model Architecture & Evaluation

weeksData.title: CMIP Experimental Design: DECK, Historical & Coordinated MIPs
days: Study standardized control, forcing, historical and coordinated model-intercomparison experiments.
Map experimental factors, controls, ensembles and response variables into a reproducible design matrix.
Compare selected multi-model fields in TraceLab while recording model, experiment, member, grid and variable metadata.
Use Sagaen Pro Art to prepare a clean experiment-design figure with a provenance record.
Defend how coordinated experiments improve comparability without eliminating shared structural limitations.

weeksData.title: CMIP7 Assessment Fast Track & Next-Generation Assessment
days: Study CMIP7's evolving sustained structure, DECK, Community MIPs and Assessment Fast Track.
Analyze how scenario, forcing, ensemble and evaluation design affect downstream assessment and uncertainty.
Prepare a TraceLab comparison plate suitable for assessment use with explicit model and experiment metadata.
Define a minimum reproducible diagnostic bundle for a hypothetical model submission using rapid-evaluation principles.
Write an assessment brief separating projection, scenario, evaluation, uncertainty and policy interpretation.

weeksData.title: Regional Climate, Dynamical & Statistical Downscaling
days: Compare dynamical downscaling, statistical downscaling, bias adjustment and regional-model nesting.
Analyze scale mismatch, stationarity, cross-validation and added-value criteria.
Compare global and regional climate fields in TraceLab, emphasizing topography and coastline effects.
Use OHMIC CAD Studio to build a nested-domain/terrain cross-section showing boundary forcing and resolution changes.
Defend a regional product by stating inherited and newly introduced uncertainty.

weeksData.title: Seasonal-to-Decadal Prediction & Predictability
days: Distinguish initialized prediction from uninitialized projection and identify sources of seasonal-to-decadal predictability.
Compute deterministic and probabilistic verification concepts including anomaly correlation and reliability.
Compare hindcast/prediction anomalies with verification fields in TraceLab.
Design a hindcast protocol with lead times, drift correction, baseline comparison and training/verification separation.
Deliver a skill briefing that avoids converting conditional predictability into deterministic certainty.

weeksData.title: Climate Extremes & Event Attribution
days: Study return periods, changing baselines, compound extremes and probabilistic event-attribution frameworks.
Analyze tail probabilities, risk ratios, confidence intervals and sensitivity to event definition.
Annotate observed and factual/counterfactual ensemble anomaly fields in TraceLab.
Design an attribution experiment and pre-register event definition, ensemble comparison and evaluation metric.
Defend an attribution statement using probability language, physical mechanism and sensitivity tests.

weeksData.title: Carbon Cycle, Biogeochemistry & Emissions-to-Concentration Response
days: Study coupled carbon pools, ocean/land uptake, airborne fraction, biogeochemical feedbacks and ESM extensions.
Build simplified multi-box carbon equations and identify conservation constraints and feedback pathways.
Trace carbon-flux, concentration or uptake fields in TraceLab with strict stock/flow distinctions.
Extend a coupled-model architecture schematic to include carbon reservoirs and exchange pathways.
Write an emissions-to-climate chain separating emissions scenario, concentration response, forcing and temperature response.
weeksData.checkpoint: Qualifying Checkpoint V · Prediction, Projection & Earth-System Modeling

weeksData.title: Ice Sheets, Sea Level & Long-Term Commitment
days: Study thermal expansion, glacier mass change, ice-sheet dynamics, gravitational fingerprints and long response times.
Analyze component sea-level contributions and uncertainty aggregation without assuming independence by default.
Annotate regional sea-level or cryosphere projection fields in TraceLab.
Use OHMIC CAD Studio to construct a coastline/ice-ocean schematic showing processes relevant to sea-level commitment.
Deliver a sea-level memo distinguishing near-term range, long-term commitment and deep uncertainty.

weeksData.title: Uncertainty Quantification & Probabilistic Projection
days: Integrate scenario, model, internal variability, parameter, observational and methodological uncertainty into a structured framework.
Use variance, covariance, conditional probability and sensitivity analysis for selected uncertainty contributions.
Annotate uncertainty maps or fan charts in TraceLab and identify dominant uncertainty by scale or horizon.
Run a Monte Carlo conceptual projection experiment and test sensitivity to distributional assumptions.
Write a probabilistic projection statement with calibrated language and a transparent uncertainty budget.

weeksData.title: Hybrid Physics–AI/ML Climate Modeling
days: Study surrogate models, emulators, learned parameterizations and hybrid physics-ML systems with scientific guardrails.
Relate regression, optimization, dimensionality reduction and dynamical constraints to climate-model ML workflows.
Compare baseline and ML/hybrid diagnostics in TraceLab, emphasizing failure patterns and out-of-distribution behavior.
Design validation with conservation checks, physical bounds, withheld regimes and reproducibility.
Defend when an ML component improves scientific utility and when predictive performance alone is insufficient.

weeksData.title: Climate Services, Risk, Decision Support & Communication
days: Translate climate information into hazards, exposure, vulnerability, risk and decision-relevant services without collapsing these concepts.
Quantify thresholds, conditional probabilities and decision metrics while separating science from value judgments.
Build a TraceLab decision-support map with uncertainty and spatial limits explicitly marked.
Use Sagaen Pro Art to produce a professional figure that remains faithful to the underlying data and provenance.
Present a stakeholder briefing stating what evidence supports, what it does not support and what choices remain outside the science.

weeksData.title: Capstone Climate Experiment, Reproducibility & Figure Suite
days: Freeze the capstone hypothesis, experiment design, variables, comparison periods, ensemble choices and falsification criteria.
Complete quantitative analysis and document every transformation, diagnostic and uncertainty decision.
Produce the principal TraceLab diagnostic suite while preserving original source layers and exportable overlays.
Use OHMIC CAD and Sagaen Pro Art only where scientifically justified for methods, architecture or communication figures.
Submit the manuscript-quality evidence package and complete a reproducibility audit.

weeksData.title: Graduate Synthesis, Assessment & Oral Defense Readiness
days: Synthesize climate dynamics, model architecture, coordinated experiments, prediction, projection and uncertainty.
Complete cumulative quantitative problems spanning dynamics, statistics, ensembles, feedbacks and evaluation.
Defend an unfamiliar climate-model diagnostic in TraceLab using only supplied evidence and metadata.
Complete a model-design/research-methods practical with conservation, reproducibility and uncertainty requirements.
Submit the capstone manuscript and complete the pre-defense oral examination before the five-gate graduate final.
weeksData.checkpoint: Qualifying Checkpoint VI · Semester II Comprehensive
